name: WHO Global Health Observatory WASH burden and coverage indicators
coverage_for_afa_countries: All 11 Aqua for All countries (Bangladesh Cambodia Ghana India Kenya Madagascar Malawi Rwanda Senegal South Africa Uganda)
indicators_relevant: WSH_1 to WSH_8 (WASH attributable deaths and DALYs 2019 incl. under five); WSH_10 and WSH_30 series (diarrhoea deaths and DALYs by water sanitation hygiene); WSH_20 series (attributable fractions by risk factor); SDGWSHBOD (SDG 3.9.2 mortality rate); WSH_WATER_BASIC WSH_WATER_SAFELY_MANAGED WSH_SANITATION_BASIC WSH_SANITATION_SAFELY_MANAGED WSH_HYGIENE_BASIC (JMP coverage series); MDG_0000000007 (under five mortality); NUTSTUNTINGPREV (stunting); HWWS_1 (handwashing after toilet)
licence: WHO data policy (open use with attribution)
what_was_pulled: 30 indicators pulled 2026-10-23 into data-raw/gho and data/country-baselines.csv (4508 rows)
notes: 2019 burden values match the WHO 2023 report annex (checked for Kenya); coverage series run to 2022

name: WHO Burden of disease attributable to unsafe WASH 2019 update (report annexes)
coverage_for_afa_countries: All 11 countries in annex tables A6 and A7 (deaths and DALYs by risk factor and age; PAFs for diarrhoea water sanitation hygiene and ARI)
indicators_relevant: Country PAFs and attributable deaths and DALYs by risk factor
what_was_pulled: Report PDF and corrigendum saved to papers/ and converted to text
notes: Same numbers as GHO WSH series; the report explains methods and counterfactuals

name: WHO Global Health Estimates 2019 (cause-specific deaths and DALYs)
indicators_relevant: Diarrhoeal disease ARI and other causes by age and sex; denominator for PAF based estimates
access: Open download (xlsx) and GHO API (GHE_DALYNUM GHE_DALYRATE)
what_was_pulled: Not pulled (GHO WSH series already carry the attributable values)
notes: Needed when the tool recomputes PAFs with user coverage scenarios

name: IHME Global Burden of Disease results tool (GBD 2021)
owner: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation
coverage_for_afa_countries: All countries and subnational for India and Kenya
indicators_relevant: Deaths DALYs YLDs for diarrhoeal diseases and burden attributable to unsafe water unsafe sanitation and no access to handwashing facility; by age sex year
access: Registration and login required to download; free of charge non-commercial user agreement; the public page returned HTTP 403 to the fetch
what_was_pulled: Not pulled (no registration as instructed); published GBD-based papers in the included set carry country values (W4411689812 W7140216878 W4401826600 W4389393005)
notes: GBD attributable fractions differ from WHO (different counterfactuals: GBD assumes larger piped water and sewer effects; see Wolf 2022 discussion)

name: WHO/UNICEF JMP global database (washdata.org) and the openwashdata jmpdata R package
owner: WHO/UNICEF JMP; openwashdata (ETH Zurich) for the package
coverage_for_afa_countries: All 11 countries with national rural urban series 2000 to 2022 (2025 release in jmpdata)
indicators_relevant: Drinking water sanitation and hygiene service ladders incl. safely managed basic limited unimproved surface water and open defecation; survey level sanitation inputs (jmpraw)
access: Open download; R package from GitHub (devtools::install_github openwashdata/jmpdata)
api_or_download: R package and CSV on GitHub; washdata.org files
what_was_pulled: Not re-pulled (GHO WSH_WATER and WSH_SANITATION series already in country-baselines.csv); jmpdata README read on GitHub
notes: jmpdata holds jmpindicators (modelled estimates with legacy JMP codes) and jmpraw (survey level sanitation); the natural source for the tool's exposure inputs and an existing openwashdata asset

name: DHS Program STATcompiler indicator API
coverage_for_afa_countries: All 11 countries (Bangladesh 1994 to 2022; Cambodia 2000 to 2021; Ghana 1988 to 2022; India 1993 to 2020; Kenya 1989 to 2022; Madagascar Malawi Rwanda Senegal South Africa Uganda surveys through 2021 or 2022)
indicators_relevant: Children under five with diarrhoea in the two weeks before the survey (CH_DIAR_C_DIA); ORT (CH_DIAT_C_ORT); improved water source and sanitation (WS_SRCE_H_IMP WS_TLET_H_IMP); handwashing place with soap and water (WS_HNDW_H_SWT); stunting (CN_NUTS_C_HA2); under five mortality (CM_ECMR_C_U5M)
access: Indicator API open without key; microdata need registration and a stated purpose (not done)
licence: DHS Program terms (indicator data free to use with citation)
what_was_pulled: 7 indicators pulled 2026-10-23 into data-raw/dhs and data/country-baselines.csv (664 rows)
notes: Diarrhoea prevalence is the only survey based morbidity baseline; two week recall; subnational breakdowns available through the API (breakdown=subnational) but not pulled

name: UNICEF Data Warehouse (SDMX API) and MICS surveys
coverage_for_afa_countries: Most of the 11 countries (MICS for Bangladesh Ghana Madagascar Malawi and others)
indicators_relevant: Diarrhoea treatment and prevalence; WASH household indicators; child mortality (UN IGME)
notes: Alternative to DHS for countries with MICS only

name: World Bank World Development Indicators
indicators_relevant: Basic and safely managed water and sanitation (SH.H2O.BASW.ZS SH.STA.BASS.ZS SH.H2O.SMDW.ZS SH.STA.SMSS.ZS SH.STA.HYGN.ZS); under five mortality; GDP per capita for valuation
what_was_pulled: Not pulled (JMP values duplicate GHO; GDP per capita needed later for valuation)
notes: Use for GDP per capita and population in the valuation step

name: UN World Population Prospects
indicators_relevant: Population by age and sex; births
access: Open download and API (key needed for the new API)
notes: Denominator for rates and for household to person conversions

name: JMP safely managed service component data (water quality testing from MICS and national surveys)
coverage_for_afa_countries: Partial (water quality modules in MICS for Bangladesh Ghana Madagascar Malawi and some national surveys)
indicators_relevant: Share of households whose drinking water is free of E coli at source and point of use; availability when needed; on premises
notes: Needed to place enterprise outputs on the safely managed ladder (the counterfactual in WHO 2023)
